# dsh-cove · DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI extension suite
English | 中文
An integrated extension suite for the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI
SSH operations · Git workbench · Browser automation · Feishu intake · Run notifications
What it is · Architecture · Features · Quick start · Documentation · Security · Community · Contribu
it is · Architecture · Features · Quick start · Documentation · Security · Community · Contributing
## What it is
dsh-cove is an extension suite for the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI. SSH operations, the Git workb
ench, Feishu intake, run-finished notifications and browser automation live in one runtime entity pl
ugin, `@dsh-cove/dsh-web-all`. Browser code is organized by DSH injection position with exactly one
module owning each position, and host capabilities are service domains under the same plugin lifecyc
le. A DSH profile mounts this single package and never patches DSH source.
The project is a developer preview: interfaces, configuration keys and internal contracts can change
between releases. See Versioning and releases.
## Architecture
- **DSH runtime**: the `dsh` CLI manages profiles, plugins, session persistence and tools; the web p
rofile is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` and this repository's `@dsh-cove/dsh-w

eb-all`.
- **One entity**: `dsh-web-all` contributes a single `web-all` row to the profile, and both

host services and browser sections share that one Cordis lifecycle.
- **Access**: the local browser
reaches `127.0.0.1:3080` directly; the remote entry needs an overlay network and the `--trusted-hos

t` fence; the desktop and mobile clients are resident shells over the same Web UI.
- **Machine value
s**: control-plane addresses, STUN endpoints and model routes never enter the repository; `config/`
injects them at build time.
## Features
### SSH remote operations
The sidebar SSH entry opens a remote operations panel. Hosts support key or password authentication
and one-click import from `~/.ssh/config`; configuration lives in `~/.dsh/dsh-ssh.json`. Configured
hosts support real operations:

- **Web terminal**: xterm.js remote terminal with live output and auto-fit;
- **File transfer**: SFT

P upload and download with progress and a remote directory browser;
- **Port forwarding**: local tun
nels into remote private services such as databases, APIs and admin consoles, bound to `127.0.0.1` o
Agent access**: the agent and the panel share one host configuration, so a request in chat can run a
the agent and the panel share one host configuration, so a request in chat can run a remote command.
### Git workbench
The right-pane Source Control workbench and the composer branch picker share one Git service domain:
switch branches, read the commit graph and inspect file changes and diffs. A branch directory (work
tree) is selected when a conversation is created; its state and cleanup actions live on the lane chi
p in the conversation header, and there is no page of its own.
### Feishu intake
The bot WebSocket inbox ships with the `lark_inbox_peek`, `lark_inbox_pop` and `lark_inbox_ack` tool
s, a credential wizard and a configuration page under Settings.
### Run-finished notifications
Every finished turn is recorded in the read-only `GET /api/dsh-notify/feed`; the desktop and mobile
machine lists read that feed, and a finished run can be pushed to Feishu once it has fully stopped.
### Browser automation
Each session gets its own Playwright browser, exposed to the agent as the `mcp__playwright__*` tool
namespace. There is no page panel: the capability exists only as tools (`launch` starts an isolated
browser, `cdp` attaches to a Chrome you started).
Configuration details for every capability live in the dsh-web-all README.
## Quick start
### Requirements

- A working DeepSeek Harness installation with `dsh web` starting normally;
- npm installs need no e
xtra tooling; installing from source needs Node.js 22 or newer and pnpm 11.
### Install with npm
For the DSH Web CLI (browser client):

1. Add the entity plugin: `dsh plugin --profile web add @dsh-cove/dsh-web-all@latest`
2. Restart the

managed `dsh web` process; every capability entry appears in the sidebar.
3. Open the Web GUI and c
onfirm the single `web-all` runtime entity is mounted.
For DSH Desktop:

1. Add the entity plugin: `dsh plugin --profile desktop add @dsh-cove/dsh-web-all@latest`
2. Verify

the profile: `dsh --profile desktop --dump-config`
3. Fully quit and reopen the desktop application.
### Install from source
The package is published on npm; a source checkout is for development and debugging only:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The profile directory is not a pnpm workspace, so `workspace:*` dependencies of `web-all` fall back
to the published npm versions; run `node scripts/link-profile.mjs` first so the profile uses the rep
ository build output.
### Runtime and published packages
A profile runtime mounts `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` and `@dsh-cove/dsh-web-
all`. The repository publishes one package:
| npm package | Shape |
| @dsh-cove/dsh-web-all | The only runtime entity; owns every host service domain and browser positi
/dsh-web-all | The only runtime entity; owns every host service domain and browser position module |
## Security
Report vulnerabilities privately through GitHub Security Advisories; never open a public issue for a
n unfixed vulnerability. SECURITY.md defines supported versions, response targets, scope, safe harbo
ur and the hardening checklist.
The plugin exposes privileged local capabilities, so its security model is part of the product: the
shared host access fence, the remote-entry invariants and the SSH, credential and account storage ru
les are documented in the dsh-web-all security model and the remote-access contract.
